text:
monitor-bot: alert: apiserver 5xx spike detected in asia1-us-east-nat-route (x10 over baseline) - severity: high
maya: seeing increased controller-manager reconcile latency too, traces point to watch queue backpressure
maya: rolling through logs now but high number of etcd leader change events in the last 6m
tj: confirmed, etcd commit latency spiking ~200ms -> apiserver times out on some list/watch calls
linh: GPU onboarding bursts earlier this morning in asia1 consumed nat ports - could be related to conntrack exhaustion
samir: can we confirm if this is region-wide or per-node? metrics show proxy fd exhaustion on proxy-nodes-asia1-a
maya: sample logs: ```E0305 09:21:12.345 apiserver.go:143] write tcp 10.3.4.5:6443: write: connection reset by peer```
maya: controller-manager logs: `I0305 09:21:14.678 controller.go:266] reconcile took 1.9s (expected <200ms)`
tj: quick check - nat conntrack usage climbed from 40%->98% between 08:50-09:15 local time, coincident with a bulk GPU attach job from infra-allocator
linh: infra-allocator run was scheduled to batch 120 GPU attaches to save on headroom costs (burst window). I can pause new attaches if needed
samir: please pause; if we let it continue apiserver availability degrades and customers notice 5xx during large inference jobs
maya: agree. Can we fail open the model routing to fallback region for high-latency calls while we remediate? That buys time for infra team
tj: I'll flip routing policy to prefer fallback eu-west1 for non-SLA traffic in 30s, push a canary first
linh: paused allocator job at 09:24:02 UTC (job id alloc-asia1-batch-2026-03-05). Monitoring nat usage now
maya: oncall-bot: create incident? brief: "APISERVER 5xx spike asia1 correlated with nat/conntrack exhaustion from GPU attach burst"
oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-031-42, severity P2, notify #incidents and #support
samir: after pause, conntrack dropped to 64% in ~3m, apiserver 5xx rate down to baseline in the last 5m
maya: next steps: (1) revert aggressive GPU attach batch window for asia1, (2) add conntrack autoscale threshold and alert, (3) add short-lived SNAT pool expansion for burst windows, (4) run postmortem focusing on cost-vs-availability of batching policy
linh: note on (1): current batching saved ~$6k/mo in egress but cost of P2 incidents may outweigh it; will propose a throttled rollout with safety checks
tj: logging action: add watchqueue depth metrics to apiserver dashboard + correlate with nat/conntrack and etcd commit latency
maya: assigning owners: lin h -> batching policy & allocator defaults, tj -> dashboards & routing fallback, samir -> apiserver probe tuning and proxy fd limits
maya: any objections to adding a temporary alert rule: conntrack usage >80% for 2m => page oncall?
samir: good call. set pager 80% for 3m window to reduce noise
linh: I'll push a follow-up PR to change default batch size and include a hard stop when conntrack >85%
maya: thanks team. I'll keep thread open for updates, but initial mitigation worked. We'll sync 10/30 for postmortem notes.
